analysis: Reviewed the landing-page changes: HomeExperience.tsx (import of publicLinks at line 13; closing CTA href changed to publicLinks.docs at line 1122), agent-resources.ts (internal markdown links changed from /developers and /contact to /developers.md and /contact.md at lines 31, 33, 54, 74 and 98), and pricing.ts (two hardcoded developer links changed to /developers.md at lines 48 and 51, seen only in the patch). These are static link and content edits to the public marketing site. They touch no provider, coordinator, attestation, key, cache, billing or authorization code, so none of the provider threat-model assets or boundaries (A-001 to A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041) are affected. The HomeExperience.tsx scroll and network-snapshot code is unchanged apart from the link edit. The /api/network fetch uses a same-origin relative URL, and the fallback snapshot is hardcoded display data. External links use rel=noreferrer. The docs link comes from a trusted constant, with no user-controlled URL injection. The .md routes are served by markdownDocuments, which is keyed on paths such as /developers and /contact. Whether the router maps /developers.md to those entries is outside the supplied evidence. That is a functional question (possible broken links), not a security one. Pricing markdown escapes model names for table-breaking characters, which this PR did not change. No security regressions identified.
